## OmniForge

**Verdict:** REQUEST_CHANGES

### Overview

Large (19-file, +1684/−886) frontend-only restyle of Perception (Reviews/Mentions/Citation Gap) and Local Presence. Colour/font token discipline in the new code is genuinely strong, but the description doesn't match the diff: it claims "UI changes only, no functionality changed," while at least five user-facing capabilities were silently removed, a brand-new pagination control is completely non-functional, and a claimed mock-removal never happened. All three independent review agents converged on the disclosure gap without prompting each other.

### At a Glance

| | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 3 |
| Important | 8 (posted inline) |
| Minor | 6 (posted inline) |

### Strengths

- Colour/font token discipline is excellent — a grep for hex/`rgba()` across all touched files matched comments only; real values resolve through theme tokens
- New tokens added symmetrically to both Pearl and Obsidian palettes with Figma-reference comments
- `designSystem.ts`'s FROZEN-file rule respected (no new exports); merge with `staging-phase` was textually clean

### Key Concerns

- **Non-functional pagination control** shipped in the Response Queue — buttons with no handlers, hardcoded "01 of 01" (see inline thread on `RespondView.tsx`)
- **Description doesn't match the diff** — "UI changes only" claimed while ≥5 capabilities were silently removed/changed (claimed-platform filter, verified badges, engine columns, reply-routing indicator, unfiltered "Read All" entry point) — see inline thread on `ReviewsTab.tsx`
- **Unrecognised citation engines render as ChatGPT's logo** — a data-accuracy regression in `mentionsShared.tsx`
- Not independently verifiable in the diff, but worth flagging here: the merge commit (`154f04b12`) failed CI type-check and both test shards before a follow-up commit fixed it — the "clean merge, green build" framing in the description doesn't reflect that. The MR description's claim that temporary mocks (`reviewsMock`, `FORCE_EXAMPLE`, `localPresenceMockData`) were removed also doesn't hold — none were actually removed (verified via `git log -S`); harmless in production since `FORCE_EXAMPLE` is dev-only, but the description is factually wrong.

### Security

No blocking security issues. Frontend-only scope confirmed (no backend/dependency changes), no injection sinks, no secrets. Two minor findings posted inline (unencoded URL param, new third-party favicon request). One additional low-confidence observation (62/100, below the posting threshold): citation URLs bound to `href` without running through this repo's existing `sanitizeURL` helper, which is already applied to identical data elsewhere in the codebase — cheap to fix, worth a look even though it didn't clear the confidence bar for its own thread.

---
*Reviewed by 3 parallel agents (MR Analyst, Codebase Reviewer, Security Reviewer)*
*Confidence threshold: 70/100 | 14 findings posted inline (of 24 total ≥70; the remaining 10 are description/commit-level observations with no corresponding diff line — see this summary's Key Concerns)*

**Critical** — MR description misrepresents the diff: undisclosed behavioural/capability changes

**What:** The MR description states "UI changes only — all workflow, functionality and backend behaviour is taken from staging-phase" and calls the diffs "presentational rewrites, not logic changes." That's not accurate. Concretely, in this file the `platforms.filter(p => p.claimed)` guard was dropped (unclaimed platforms now render where they previously didn't) and `onViewReviews` changed from "open all reviews" to "open reviews filtered by platform." Elsewhere in the same MR, undisclosed: the "Cited by Engines" column and the Citation Gap Rivals/Priority columns were deleted, the ✓ verified badge was removed from Acquisition's recent-review cards, the reply-routing indicator ("Opens {platform}" vs "Replies in CLEO") was removed from RespondView, the only unfiltered "Read All Reviews →" entry point was removed twice, and per-platform accent colours were dropped in favour of one uniform gold.

**Why it matters:** A reviewer trusting the description will approve real functional/data-visibility changes believing they're a repaint. None of the above got a product decision — they got a styling rubber-stamp.

**Recommendation:**
Either revert the behavioural changes into a separate MR, or rewrite the description to enumerate every one of them explicitly (with before/after screenshots) and get explicit product sign-off before merge.

Confidence: 100/100 | Found by: MR Analyst, Codebase Reviewer, Security Reviewer (all three independently)

**Important** — Local Presence tab-bar restyle is dark-mode only

**What:** The author's own comment says "Dark-only — the stroke is a dark Figma hex, so Pearl keeps the default styling." The active-tab stroke/label treatment is gated entirely on `isDark`, with no Pearl branch.

**Why it matters:** This directly contradicts both the MR description's "both Pearl (light) and Obsidian (dark) modes are covered" claim and this repo's styling rule that every new/touched UI component must work correctly in both modes. The same MR correctly added Pearl analogues for five other new tokens — the pattern was known, just not applied here.

**Recommendation:**
Add Pearl analogues for `border.rangeActive` / `text.tabActiveLabel` in `theme.ts` (mirroring the other five tokens added in this diff) and resolve via the same per-mode pattern instead of the `isDark ? {...} : {}` conditional spread.

Confidence: 100/100 | Found by: MR Analyst, Codebase Reviewer (independently confirmed on the same lines)

**Important** — Pearl (light mode) contrast regression on active tab label

**What:** The new `activeLabelColor` override (also applied at `Reviews/ReviewsTab.tsx:252`) resolves to `#5C5C5C` for Pearl's active label, which is barely distinguishable from the existing inactive label colour `#6B655A`. Dark mode is fine (`#B7B7B7` active vs. `~#737373` inactive).

**Why it matters:** In Pearl the selected sub-tab loses its label-colour signal — only the faint pill background distinguishes it. This is exactly the light-mode-only failure mode the repo's styling rule exists to prevent.

**Recommendation:**
The Figma value `#B7B7B7` is a dark-surface grey; the Pearl analogue should preserve contrast ratio against the Pearl pill background rather than mirroring the raw hex lightness — something around `#3A3A3A` would restore adequate contrast.

Confidence: 90/100 | Found by: Codebase Reviewer

**Important** — Global `'&& *'` font-weight override breaks existing component tokens

**What:** Five page roots (this file, plus `MentionsOverview.tsx:147`, `Reviews/RespondView.tsx:119`, `Reviews/ReviewsDirectories.tsx:87`, `Reviews/AcquisitionView.tsx:84`) apply `'&& *': { fontWeight: agencyTypography.fontWeight.regular }` at doubled specificity. This outranks any descendant's own `sx`, including deliberately-bold shared tokens — confirmed: `getAgencyOutlineGoldButtonSx`'s `fontWeight: medium` is silently discarded on the "Open outreach board →" button and the Inclusion Gate CTA rendered inside these subtrees.

**Why it matters:** Shared design tokens no longer mean what they say inside these five subtrees, and any future child that legitimately needs bold text can't get it without an `!important` fight. Not disclosed as a trade-off anywhere in the MR description.

**Recommendation:**
Apply `fontWeight: regular` directly on the ~15 style helpers in `reviewsStyles.ts` that need it (most already do this correctly) and drop the blanket descendant selector from all five page shells.

Confidence: 100/100 | Found by: MR Analyst (disclosure gap), Codebase Reviewer (concrete token breakage) — same root cause, independently found

**Important** — Hardcoded rgba() colours replace token-derived values

**What:** `localPageCategoryBadgeSx` changed from `hexToRgba(c.accent.gold, ...)` / a token-derived stroke to raw `rgba(255,255,255,0.04)` / `rgba(0,0,0,0.03)` literals.

**Why it matters:** This is the only place in the entire 19-file diff with hardcoded colours — everywhere else genuinely resolves through theme tokens (verified by grep across all touched files). It directly contradicts both the repo's styling rule (never hardcode hex/rgba values) and this MR's own "no hardcoded colours" claim, and these two colour pairs won't follow any future theme/palette change.

**Recommendation:**
Use the existing neutral-overlay pattern instead, e.g. `alpha(c.text.primary, 0.04)` / `c.border.default`, or add explicit `pearl`/`obsidian` tokens for a neutral chip wash in `theme.ts`.

Confidence: 95/100 | Found by: Codebase Reviewer

**Important** — Test suite regression guards silently defanged

**What:** This test was flipped from asserting an engine pill renders (`getByText('ChatGPT')`) to asserting it does not — but `MentionsOverview.tsx` no longer renders `EnginePills` at all, so this (and two other tests in the same file, the "empty engines array" and "R8 DOM restructure / anchor" tests) now pass tautologically, for reasons unrelated to what their names claim to verify.

**Why it matters:** The suite reports green while its actual regression coverage for SC-2 and R8 is gone — a future reintroduction of either bug would ship silently. There's also no test anywhere for this MR's headline change (engine logos via `getLLMIcon`), including no coverage of the unknown-engine fallback flagged separately as a Critical finding.

**Recommendation:**
Delete or rewrite the now-vacuous tests, and add a `mentionsShared.test.tsx` asserting `EnginePills`/`getLLMIcon` renders one icon per known engine, an em-dash for `[]`, and does **not** silently render the ChatGPT mark for an unrecognised engine name.

Confidence: 96/100 | Found by: MR Analyst, Codebase Reviewer (independently confirmed)

**Important** — Shared accessible tab-switch replaced with inaccessible hand-rolled buttons

**What:** The sentiment filter was migrated off the shared `SiteWorkspaceTabSwitch` component onto bare `Box component="button"` pills with no `aria-pressed` / `role="tab"` / `aria-selected`. Selected state is now conveyed by colour alone.

**Why it matters:** This is invisible to screen readers, and it's an odd choice given this exact MR *extends* `SiteWorkspaceTabSwitch` elsewhere with a new `activeLabelColor` prop — the shared, accessible component was clearly still viable here.

**Recommendation:**
Use `SiteWorkspaceTabSwitch` (now that it supports `activeLabelColor`) for this filter too, or at minimum add `aria-pressed={filter === f.id}` to each hand-rolled button.

Confidence: 88/100 | Found by: MR Analyst, Codebase Reviewer (independently confirmed)

**Minor** — Unencoded URL parameter + new third-party data channel

**What:** `m.domain` (a backend-supplied value, not guaranteed to be a bare hostname) is interpolated into the Google favicon URL without `encodeURIComponent`, diverging from 7 other call sites in this codebase that do encode it. Separately, this is a genuinely new outbound request — previously this table rendered engine names as text with zero external requests; now every card fetches from `google.com`, carrying the domain plus the viewer's Google cookies/Referer.

**Why it matters:** A domain containing `&` or `#` mangles the query string and silently drops the favicon (low severity — the host is hardcoded, so this isn't a redirect/SSRF vector). The new Google request is a minor confidentiality consideration worth a conscious decision rather than a side effect of a restyle.

**Recommendation:**
```tsx
src={`https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=${encodeURIComponent(m.domain)}&sz=64`}
```
Consider also adding `referrerPolicy="no-referrer"`, or proxying favicons through the backend / rendering a first-party letter avatar as `LocalPresence` does elsewhere.

Confidence: 88/100 | Found by: Security Reviewer, Codebase Reviewer (independently confirmed on the same line)

**Minor** — Dead ternary with identical branches

**What:** `background: hexToRgba(c.accent.gold, isDark ? 0.1 : 0.1)` — both branches resolve to the same value.

**Why it matters:** Reads as an intentional per-mode difference that doesn't exist; a future edit to one branch will silently diverge from the other without anyone noticing why they're different.

**Recommendation:**
```ts
background: hexToRgba(c.accent.gold, 0.1),
```

Confidence: 90/100 | Found by: Codebase Reviewer

**Minor** — Magic numbers contradict the file's own "no hardcoded values" claim

**What:** This file's header comment (and the MR description) states every value resolves from the theme with no hardcoded colours, fonts, or magic numbers. In practice a dozen Figma-derived literals remain: `letterSpacing: '0.8px'` (here and at line 626), plus others (`'0.5px'`, `'-1px'`, fixed pixel heights, `borderRadius: '3px'`) scattered through the file.

**Why it matters:** Not a functional defect — colour/font sourcing genuinely is clean throughout this file — but the claim as written is falsifiable, and the repo's styling rule explicitly calls out "magic numbers pulled from a plan/mockup."

**Recommendation:**
Either soften the header comment to scope the claim to colours/fonts, or promote the recurring letterSpacing/height values into a shared `agencyTypography.letterSpacing` / `reviewsMetrics` token object.

Confidence: 78/100 | Found by: Codebase Reviewer
